commit.message: docs: add release notes entry for aux sig validation

lnwallet: require an aux sig per HTLC on taproot overlay channels

The aux signature blob is peer supplied and carries no count of its own.
Verification jobs were only built for HTLCs an entry was received for,
so a peer could withhold the aux signature for an HTLC simply by
omitting it: no job was produced, nothing reported the omission, and the
commitment became our state carrying a signature we never received. At
force close the resolver then reads an empty signature out of that
HTLC's custom records, and the second level HTLC cannot be swept.

An aux signer emits exactly one entry per non-dust HTLC, in lockstep
with the BTC level signatures, so the count is now checked the same way
those already are, right beside them.

The check is gated on the tapscript root bit rather than merely on an
aux signer being configured. The signer is attached node wide, so it is
also present on plain channels, whose peers correctly send no aux
signatures at all, and requiring them there would force close those
channels. That bit is set at funding time if and only if the negotiated
commitment type is a taproot overlay, so it names exactly the channels
whose peers owe us aux signatures.

lnwallet: model the aux sig blob faithfully in tests

Three places modelled the aux signature blob less faithfully than
production does, in ways that hid whether the blob was carried at all.

MockAuxSigner.UnpackSigs returned a single slot no matter how many HTLCs
were packed. A real aux signer emits exactly one slot per HTLC, and code
that pairs the unpacked slots with HTLCs by index depends on that. The
default mock now records the slot count in the packed blob and hands
back that many slots. Since the blob is parsed into custom records, it
has to stay a canonical TLV stream, so the count travels in the dummy
record's value. Registering a function rather than a fixed value is what
lets the result depend on the input.

restartChannel rebuilt the channel with no channel options, so a restart
silently dropped the aux signer and the restarted side stopped producing
aux signatures while its peer still expected them. Production re-applies
the aux components every time a channel is loaded.

Two chan sync tests rebuilt CommitSigs from a retransmitted wire message
without its aux signature blob, which the link carries across.

docs: add release note for the offer store

Add the offer store to the BOLT 12 section of the 0.22.0 release notes.
The PR link holds a placeholder until the PR number is known.

offers: add offer store with insert and lookup

Introduce the offers package with a SQL-backed store for BOLT 12 offers.
The store keeps the encoded offer and the local state that the offer
string does not carry. It has an insert and a lookup by offer hash.
CreateOffer validates the parameters, encodes the offer and inserts it.

commit.message:
sqldb: add offer store schema

Add the offers table migration and its generated sqlc queries. Offers
are long-lived reusable templates, a lifecycle with no BOLT 11 analog,
so they get their own table rather than extending invoices.

The table keeps the encoded offer and the local state only. The lno1
string is the content, and it never changes after creation. The local
state is the data that no offer or invoice request carries: the
disabled flag and the creation time. No column holds a typed copy of an
offer field.

This is enough because the invoice request carries the offer terms.
The payer copies every offer field into the request, and the offer hash
covers the whole offer range. A lookup by that hash therefore proves an
exact match, so a spec extension needs no migration.

The hash is UNIQUE, which also indexes it for the lookup. The queries
are the insert and the lookup by hash, the two the offer store calls.

A table with one row per TLV record was also considered. It needs a
query over many rows per offer, and it loses the column types.

The migration is a development migration. It is in migrationAdditions,
so only builds with the SQL test tags apply it, and a normal build does
not change the user's schema. The offers schema can still change before
the receive flow is complete. When it is final, the migration moves to
the main line with the next free versions.

Review: https://github.com/lightningnetwork/lnd/pull/11278#issuecomment-5941177626

commit.message:
lnwire: fix NodeAnnouncement2 address aliasing

The address decoders declared their scratch arrays outside the address
loop, so every decoded net.TCPAddr held a slice over the same backing
array. Each pass overwrote the addresses already appended, and the list
collapsed onto the last address read.

A message carrying 1.2.3.4:8080 and 5.6.7.8:8081 decoded as
5.6.7.8:8080 and 5.6.7.8:8081. The first address was lost. IPv6
behaved the same way. Tor v3 was immune because EncodeToString copies
the bytes into a string. We fix this by allocating within the address
loop iteration, even for tor to be consistent.

We update rapid tests to include several addresses.

lnwire: fix NodeAnnouncement2 short reads

The io.Reader contract lets a reader return fewer bytes than the caller
asked for with a nil error. The IPv4, IPv6 and Tor v3 address decoders
called Read for their fixed width fields and ignored the returned count,
so the untouched zero bytes of the scratch array became address data.

A 5 byte frame that declares a 6 byte IPv4 record decoded as
1.2.3.4:7936 with no error. io.ReadFull makes the short read an
io.ErrUnexpectedEOF.

The TLV format does not change and no complete valid record is rejected.

commit.message: docs: add release notes for migrate driver fix

sqldb/v2: close the Postgres migrate driver after use

The sqldb/v2 Postgres store has the same leak as sqldb. The pgx migrate
driver takes one connection from the pool it gets, and it keeps that
connection until the driver is closed. executeMigrations,
GetSchemaVersion and SetSchemaVersion used the shared pool and never
closed the driver, so each call held one connection for the life of the
store.

Each driver now gets its own database handle from the same DSN, and the
caller closes the driver. Closing the driver closes that handle and
leaves the shared pool open. A failed close is logged.

TestPostgresMigrateDriverReleasesConns is the same test as in sqldb.

sqldb: close the Postgres migrate driver after use

The pgx migrate driver takes one connection from the pool it gets, and
it keeps that connection until the driver is closed. ExecuteMigrations,
GetSchemaVersion and SetSchemaVersion used the shared pool and never
closed the driver. Each schema migration therefore held one connection
for the life of the store.

A fresh database runs 18 schema migration steps plus one schema version
read, so the store keeps 19 connections after startup. With the default
pool of 25, only 6 connections stay free. If db.postgres.maxconnections
is lower than 20, the migrations wait forever for a free connection,
and lnd does not start.

Each driver now gets its own database handle from the same DSN, and
the caller closes the driver. Closing the driver closes that handle and
leaves the shared pool open. A failed close is logged.

TestPostgresMigrateDriverReleasesConns checks that the schema version
calls leave no connection in use, both in the pool and on the server.
The server count is necessary because each driver uses its own handle,
which the pool stats do not include. TestPostgresMigrationSmallConnPool
runs all migrations on a fresh database with a pool of two connections,
under a one minute deadline. It reproduces the startup hang from #11007.

Co-authored-by: Vandit Singh <vanditsinghkv@gmail.com>
